gen-dafont-cheri-fs-epilogue: Epilogue reads soft and curvy, its wiry strokes loose and friendly. Cheri's calligraphic hand sits above it, sturdy and tall, so the page gets one voice that flourishes and another that simply talks.
gen-dafont-cheri-fs-public-sans: Cute and sturdy, Cheri writes with a calligraphic hand and no thin hairlines at all, while Public Sans carries a hefty, broad-countered lowercase. Give Cheri the bigger size.
gen-dafont-cheri-general-sans: Cheri's most striking habit is its tall, sturdy lowercase, written in a calligraphic hand with no hairlines to thin it out. Use it big and brief, and let General Sans handle the rest.
gen-dafont-cheri-satoshi: Cheri brings an inviting, cute calligraphic hand, its tall lowercase making every word look sturdy and large. Satoshi follows in approachable sans-serif, with a soaring x-height and an e that never squeezes shut.
gen-dafont-cheri-work-sans: Inviting is the first word for Cheri's calligraphic hand. Work Sans sits beside it in a modern plain sans, crisp and high-lined, so the script feels even warmer.
gen-dafont-college-gf-julius-sans-one: Authoritative and dynamic, College packs big counters into a tall lowercase with curves as heavy as its stems. Julius Sans One simply stretches out, light and spacious, with minimal gap between capitals and lowercase.
gen-dafont-college-gf-lexend-exa: Authoritative College hits hard, with curves as thick as its straight stems and big counters throughout. Lexend Exa is the foil: a sans with stubby ascenders and wide, distinct curves under a big x-height.
gen-dafont-college-gf-lexend-giga: Heavy curves and tall, open counters give College real punch up top. Lexend Giga is a plain sans with flat, single-weight linework, and its generous tracking lets each word breathe beneath that weight.
gen-dafont-college-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega looks drawn with one nib, its body height nearly matching the capitals and a clear gap at every c. Nudge it up in size while College stays as it is.
gen-dafont-college-gf-lexend-peta: Lexend Peta reads professional and approachable, with unthinned curves and c shapes like a wide mouth. College hits harder, yet Lexend Peta keeps pace, a sans-serif whose big x-height matches the heading's tall, open lowercase.
